sn46.52:5.1: “Sir, we robed up in the morning and, taking our bowls and robes, entered Sāvatthī for alms.
sn46.52:5.3: ‘It’s too early to wander for alms in Sāvatthī.
sn46.52:5.4: Why don’t we visit the monastery for the wanderers of other religions?’
sn46.52:5.5: Then we went to the monastery for the wanderers of other religions and exchanged greetings with the wanderers there.
sn46.52:5.6: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, we sat down to one side. The wanderers said to us:
sn46.52:6.1: ‘Reverends, the ascetic Gotama teaches his disciples like this: “Mendicants, please give up the five hindrances—corruptions of the heart that weaken wisdom—and truly develop the seven awakening factors.”
sn46.52:6.3: “Reverends, please give up the five hindrances—corruptions of the heart that weaken wisdom—and truly develop the seven awakening factors.”
sn46.52:6.4: What, then, is the difference between the ascetic Gotama’s teaching and instruction and ours?’
sn46.52:7.1: Then we neither approved nor rejected that statement of the wanderers of other religions. We rose from our seats, thinking:
sn46.52:7.2: ‘We will learn the meaning of this statement from the Buddha himself.’”
